page: Google Cloud Platform c3d-standard-8-lssd is a general-purpose virtual machine instance featuring the x86_64 architecture. It is powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 9B14 processor with 8 vCPUs, which map to 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core. The system is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB per core. Storage is bundled as a single local NVMe SSD with a capacity of 402 GB, while no GPU accelerators are present on this instance type.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong single-core capabilities, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance and Geekbench text processing both scoring in the top 25%. Most standard compute workloads, including multi-core CPU execution, software compilation, and static web serving, fall within the average range. However, a notable hardware tradeoff exists in memory subsystem performance; while small-block cached read bandwidth is average, large-block uncached read bandwidth is weak, and large-block write bandwidth falls into the bottom 10% of tested systems.

Given its balanced CPU-to-memory ratio and dedicated AMD EPYC cores, this instance offers moderate resource density for general-purpose workloads. The inclusion of a local NVMe SSD provides low-latency storage, making it suitable for database operations, web serving, and text processing tasks that do not require massive memory bandwidth. It represents a standard qualitative cost-to-performance option for environments requiring dedicated compute resources and local scratch space without the overhead of high-end memory-optimized or GPU-accelerated hardware.
